sections.h2: Where to record a Johnston County deed
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is on the ground floor of the Smithfield courthouse, Suite 209 at 207 E. Johnston Street, near the 2nd and Market Street corner of Courthouse Square. Call 919-989-5160 for land records.

The office is open weekdays except county holidays, and the real estate counter takes walk-ins without an appointment until 4:45 p.m. Vital records have their own line, 919-989-5161. An heir who needs a death certificate for an estate sale should use that number.

In North Carolina, priority follows the time a document is registered in the county where the land sits. A signed deed that never gets recorded leaves the buyer exposed to a later purchaser or a lien creditor. The usual plan is to record on the day the buyer funds.

A plain deed costs a flat $26.00 through page 15, and each extra page adds $4.00. A deed of trust or mortgage has a longer base, $64.00 through page 35.

Johnston County recording charges
Document or serviceCharge
Deed, easement or similar instrument$26.00 up to page 15, extra pages at $4.00 each
Home loan security instrument (deed of trust or mortgage)$64.00 up to page 35, extra pages at $4.00 each
Release of a security instrumentNone
Document that breaks the formatting rules$25.00
Plat map$21.00 a page
Fax, local call10 cents a page

If you mail a package and are owed a refund of $1.00 or less, none is sent. Anything larger comes back as a check from county finance.

The excise stamp is $2.00 per $1,000 of consideration, which the office also writes as $1.00 per $500. The seller pays it. State law puts the burden on the transferor, and it is due at the register's counter before the deed is recorded.

Half the money goes to the county general fund and half to the Department of Revenue. The stamp is a separate line from the per-page fee, and the closing company normally puts both in the seller column of the settlement statement.

Because the rate applies to each $500 or part of $500, ask the office or your closing attorney for the exact stamp on your contract price before closing day.

sections.h2: Can a Johnston County deed be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. Johnston County was among the first in North Carolina to e-record every document type, and among the first anywhere to e-record plat maps. Most of what the office receives now comes in electronically.

The approved submitters are:

  • CSC eRecording
  • EPN
  • Indecomm
  • NTC
  • Simplifile

After recording, the document goes back to the submitter within seconds for review. Title companies and closing attorneys usually have an account with one of these services, so a seller rarely logs in. If you close without a lawyer, ask whoever handles your closing which service they use and when the file can go out.

The county also runs an online search. You can look up a grantor or grantee name, a reception number, a date range or a subdivision, and a find-related function pulls up documents that share a legal description.

Three things add to the total, and each has its own line on the schedule.

  • Length. Every page past 15 on a deed adds $4.00.
  • Bundled instruments. A document containing two or more instruments with different legal effect adds $10.00 for each extra one.
  • Format. A paper that fails the state recording standards draws another $25.00.

Payoff paperwork is the cheap part. A satisfaction, trustee's satisfaction or affidavit of satisfaction carries no charge, so clearing an old loan costs nothing at the register. If your lender has not released its lien, ask it to send the satisfaction for recording right after payoff.

sections.h2: Before the deed goes to the register
sections.html:
Have the deed signed, notarized and complete before it leaves the closing table. The register records instruments and does not draft or repair them.

Run through this list before the signing appointment ends:

  • Match the grantor names to the way title is held today.
  • Copy the parcel description from your own deed.
  • Work out the stamp amount the seller will pay.
  • Ask your lender to record a satisfaction of the old deed of trust.
  • Ask the Johnston County tax office about any unpaid bill, since the property tax lien attaches to a parcel on the January 1 listing date.

The office also offers a free fraud alert, which you join through the county website. Owners who rent out a house or leave it empty during a sale may want it, since the office reports property fraud cases on the rise.

Estate paperwork belongs to the clerk of court, and the register only records the deeds that follow. Smaller estates have a shortcut: once 30 days have gone by since the death, an heir, creditor or public administrator can file an affidavit if personal property net of liens does not exceed $20,000.

The register keeps the lien index but removes nothing by itself. A mortgage or deed of trust leaves the record only when a satisfaction is recorded. Tax liens work differently. They attach to the parcel on its January 1 listing date, and collection is a court foreclosure.

A house with liens, back taxes, tenants or repair needs can still sell for cash without a listing or showings. The deed goes to this same register and carries the same recording fee and stamp as any other sale.

A smooth recording depends on what happens before the deed reaches Suite 209. Most sales follow the same order.

  1. The closing attorney or title company reviews the deed for the right grantor names and parcel description.
  2. You sign in front of a notary, and the buyer funds the purchase.
  3. The seller's excise stamp is collected as part of the settlement figures.
  4. The file is sent to the register through one of the approved e-recording services, or carried to the counter before 4:45 p.m.
  5. The office records the deed, and the submitter receives the recorded copy back within seconds.
  6. Your old lender records its satisfaction, which costs nothing, and you keep a copy for your files.

If you are selling without an attorney, ask your title company who will handle recording and when. A deed that misses the afternoon cutoff waits until the next business day, and priority follows the time of registration, so timing counts.

Johnston County sits east of Raleigh and has grown fast, with a population of 256,448 and about 99,408 housing units. A typical owned home is worth $305,600, and 76.1 percent of households are owner-occupied. Builders pulled 3,002 permits in 2025, so new houses compete with resales and buyers of older homes often ask for repairs or credits.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Johnston County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Dial 919-989-5160 for land records, or 919-989-5161 for vital records and marriage licenses. The office is in Suite 209 at 207 E. Johnston Street, Smithfield.

faqs.q: How much does a standard Johnston County deed cost to record?
faqs.a: A plain deed runs $26.00 up to page 15, with $4.00 added for each later page. Loan paperwork is priced higher, $64.00 up to page 35. The stamp is a separate charge.

faqs.q: Is there a charge for recording a satisfaction in Johnston County?
faqs.a: No. Satisfactions of a security instrument, trustee's satisfactions, notices, certificates and affidavits of satisfaction are recorded at no charge.

faqs.q: Is e-recording available for Johnston County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes, through an approved submitter. CSC eRecording, EPN, Indecomm, NTC and Simplifile are on the list, and your closing company normally sends the file for you.

faqs.q: Whose job is it to pay the transfer stamp in Johnston County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it at the register's counter while the deed is still unrecorded. The rate is $2.00 per $1,000 of consideration.
